| [CLAIM-351](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-351.md) | A zero aggregate gradient does not show that the demands it aggregates are reconciled: with positive weights it holds both when every demand's own gradient vanishes and when nonzero gradients cancel, and in the second case no update improves them all to first order; even the first is only joint first-order stationarity, which a demand's maximum or saddle also has | A33 §5 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "Zero aggregate gradient does not imply absence of frustrated demands." With L₁ = (θ − 1)² and L₂ = (θ + 1)² at θ = 0 ([CASE-115](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-115.md)), the equal-weight gradient is zero and the aggregate is at its global minimum, while each loss is 1 and wants the opposite move. | [CLAIM-365](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md) | On a norm-ball update set the local frustration residual Φ_r = min over ‖d‖ ≤ r of max_i(ε_i + g_iᵀd) equals the maximum over the simplex of Σλ_iε_i − r‖Σλ_ig_i‖_*, so infeasibility of the declared improvements has a certificate, and any admissible actual update exceeds Φ_r by a nonnegative governance regret | A34 §4 and A35 §3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, checked. The residual is the smallest worst-case shortfall of the declared local improvements ε_i over updates of size at most r. Minimax for the bilinear problem on two compact convex sets gives the dual over the simplex, so Φ_r > 0 exactly when some λ certifies that no update meets all demands (A34's form). Governance regret Γ is the gap between an actual admissible update's shortfall and Φ_r, and is never negative. For L₁ = (θ − 1)², L₂ = (θ + 1)² at θ = 0, Φ_r = ε for every r. The sharp edge: per A37 it is a cardinal refinement of the ordinal fact ([CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)), and its magnitude depends on units (A36 §2D). | Active |
| [CLAIM-366](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-366.md) | Whether several objectives share a strict first-order descent direction, 0 ∉ conv{g_i}, is invariant under smooth invertible reparameterization, while the sign of a Euclidean gradient inner product is not, and a negative inner product does not exclude common descent; a budgeted version is invariant only with the metric pulled back | A35 §2 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, at the owner's U35 "double click" on whether functionally equivalent parameterizations give equivalent frustration diagnoses. Gradients transform as g′ = Jᵀg and directions as v′ = J⁻¹v, so directional derivatives, and with them the common-descent test 0 ∉ conv{g_i}, do not depend on coordinates. A Euclidean inner product does: g₁ = (1, 1), g₂ = (1, −½) have product ½, and under θ = diag(½, 2)ψ their transforms have −7/4, while d = (−1, 0) lowers both throughout. The sharp edge: it covers coordinate changes of one parameter space at first order, not function-preserving symmetries or training trajectories ([QUESTION-127](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-127.md)). The practice corollary, not to diagnose task conflict by gradient cosine, is the anthology's. | Active |
